# CICS crucible: where the pipeline stands

<!-- Generated by tests/tools/cics_crucible.py --update-baseline; do not edit by hand. -->

Measured against [cics-crucible](https://github.com/squid-protocol/cics-crucible) at `v0.1.0 (0c942cb8)` (tests/_cics_crucible_pin.py). Epic #3989. Each case of the crucible is a small CICS application whose scenarios carry a hand-written expected event log, derived from IBM's documentation. Here is how the pipeline's output compares with those logs, cell by cell. A cell is one side of one scenario: **engine-facts** (per case: the scan recorded its programs, transactions, maps and CICS commands), **forge-compile** (per case: the generated Spring Boot project compiles), **cobol-stub** (the COBOL on the harness's stub CICS runtime) and **java** (the generated services, task by task through `CicsTask`). A cell passes, fails at its first divergence from the log, or is *unsupported*: the harness cannot model something the scenario needs yet. The comparison is exact (SPEC 6).

Every cell that does not pass is ledgered in `tests/cics_crucible/baseline.json`, and CI (`cics-crucible.yml`) holds the ledger as a ratchet.

## Harness work, in the order that unlocks the most cells

Each missing feature belongs to a piece of harness work (below: the features themselves). A cell is *unlocked* when every piece its features need is done: it then gets a pass or fail verdict rather than `unsupported`. **needs** counts the cells that do not pass and need the piece, **alone** the unsupported cells it unlocks by itself, and **cumulative** the unsupported cells unlocked by it and every row above it (rows are chosen greedily).
